We investigate the semi-inclusive $B\to X_s\ell^+\ell^-$ process with $\ell$
being either electron or muon, focusing on the ratio $R_{LFV}$ that compares
lepton-flavor-specific to overall $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ branching fractions.
Our study is conducted across multiple theoretical frameworks, utilizing both
pole and four-momentum transfer squared ($q^2$) formalisms. We find that if
the standard model is correct, $R_{LFV}$ should be approximately $0.31\%$ at
low-$q^2$, significantly below the sensitivity threshold of upcoming $B$-physics
experiments. However, if certain flavor-changing neutral current processes
occur at next-to-leading order, a non-zero $R_{LFV}$ value could arise,
potentially emerging at the same rate as its standard model counterpart.

This work delves into decentralized regulation problems involving linear, multi-channel networks, exploring connections to convex and concave programming. A new architecture is proposed, comprising augmented sum-link and sum-square summation functions, which allows for the scalable expansion and reorganization of the network without affecting convergence. Furthermore, the proposed methods exhibit plug-and-play capability, meaning their effectiveness is not compromised by the introduction of new modules. Notably, the methods can easily be adapted to estimate channel states and signals using layer-wise output. The paper demonstrates the benefits of its approaches via simulation examples comparing their performance with existing solutions.

To combat the rapidly spreading COVID-19 virus, researchers are exploring ways to analyze articles from clinical and molecular biology sources to gain a deeper understanding of the disease. A novel two-phase approach has been developed to categorize COVID-19 articles into relevant fields such as law, medicine, and communication. This involved constructing a new dataset, which serves as the foundation for training a BERT model to classify articles effectively. In the first phase, the model is trained on a large dataset to distinguish clinical from molecular biology articles, utilizing specific keywords extracted through the Tfidf algorithm. While this resulted in high fidelity and accurate classification of major fields, it struggled with detecting subtle sub-fields. To address this limitation, a second phase was introduced, employing a set of predefined keywords to filter out sub-fields. This approach successfully categorized all COVID-19 articles into specific fields. Furthermore, the model's exceptional performance on the smaller sub-field dataset highlights the significant progress made in this area.

This paper presents a freely available, regularly updated guide providing research students and newcomers to the field with a comprehensive overview of network fundamentals, theoretical frameworks, analysis methods, and cutting-edge research areas, emphasizing practical application and real-world relevance.

The study of eco-evolutionary dynamics has significantly broadened the conventional view of the process, yet the influence of time scales ranging from centuries to generations remains under reviewed. To address this gap, the current research is centered on ancient eco-evolutionary scenarios, including cases where the rate of demographic processes outpaces generations from a genetic and ecological standpoint. Our analysis shows that the length of these time scales, characterized as 'durations', has a profound impact on the evolution of specific eco-evolutionary models. Consequently, a new method is introduced to classify 'durations' and a comprehensive framework is developed to analyze and understand non-genetic factors influencing eco-evolutionary dynamics. This method extends beyond traditional classification systems, encompassing scenarios where the rate of non-genetic factors outpaces generations. Key findings show that the evolution of specific eco-evolutionary models is heavily reliant on time scale characteristics but may also feature abrupt, predictable changes, especially when the rate of non-genetic factors surpasses generations. This is particularly true for the 'thermal' eco-evolutionary dynamics, an essential model in the study of the process. In contrast, scenarios where 'durations' outpace generations are characterized by the relative stability of various eco-evolutionary dynamics, including models featuring monostability, bistability, and multistability. A decentralized, decentralized exchange, operating without the intermediation of a central authority, provides key benefits to participants, including the elimination of fees, enhanced security, and resilience to operational disruptions. The proliferation of Smart Contract-powered decentralized exchanges has been fueled by the growth in use of Blockchain technology. However, despite their popularity, most existing platforms have proven to be flawed, with several key shortcomings. Chiefly, they fail to effectively manage order flows, resulting in suboptimal prices for buyers and sellers. Furthermore, they neglect to address concerns related to security and robustness, leaving them exposed to potential risks. In an effort to address these limitations, we introduce the concept of BlockChain-powered decentralized exchanges (BCDEs), which provide a foundational framework for their design. By incorporating established computer science concepts such as VCG pricing, priority queues, and task duplication, BCDEs aim to optimize performance and ensure reliable operation. By leveraging BCDEs, participants can expect to see improved price outcomes and more efficient transaction processing.

A new statistical approach has been developed to evaluate the reliability of associations between health factors and specific outcomes, especially when there is limited data available. This method builds upon the existing 'E-value' method but incorporates a Bayesian calculation to assess the impact of missing data. Utilizing a sensitivity parameter (lambda) that controls the impact of missing information, the proposed method can be applied in two forms. These variants aim to address two key questions: Can we trust the findings if missing data is taken into consideration? And Can we trust the findings if missing data is not considered? To answer these questions, the method calculates an 'E-value' that determines if there is evidence of an association risk. This approach has been demonstrated through a hypothetical example focusing on asthma exposure and health risks in schools.

The widespread use of internet in education has brought many advantages, yet it also poses a risk of data security breaches. To address this challenge, countries have developed data protection laws, though the current educational system faces difficulties in complying with these laws. Moreover, the integration of internet of things (IoT) in education has complicated the issue of data privacy. A potential solution to these problems is the implementation of a federated learning-enabled blockchain system in the context of IoT. This method has the capability to comply with protection laws and maintain data privacy. A systematic literature survey on blockchain-enabled federated learning frameworks in education is presented, focusing on their applications, advantages, and future developments. To enhance the reliability of these systems, two case studies are considered: ensuring a blockchain-enabled FL system can properly train models across multiple schools, and developing a secure mechanism for verifying FL-related data using digital certificates and public key infrastructure (PKI).

The ALICE experiment measures the production of non-prompt and direct D mesons in proton-proton collisions at 5.02 TeV, and then categorizes the data based on the number of charged particles produced in the collision. The measurement, which covers D zero, D-one and D-two mesons, reveals that charm is formed predominantly at a center-of-mass rapidity between 2.5 and 4.0. The research further assesses the role of nuclear interactions in the creation of such charm. The findings are then compared with theoretical models, which predict that nuclear interactions increase the production of certain charged particles even in small systems. Notably, the data suggests that the fragmentation of quarks and antiquarks contributes significantly to the formation of non-prompt and direct D mesons.

The escalating demand for reliable quantum computing systems prompts an urgent need for advanced cold electronics and cryogenic manufacturing capable of withstanding the rigorous conditions necessary for operating topological qubits and other quantum computing components. This study describes the development of a cutting-edge platform for quantum computing that incorporates cutting-edge materials, cryogenic electronics, and cryogenic microwave engineering to create a sophisticated interface for quantum computing components. The interface, which operates in the millikelvin temperature range, features three user-defined sample slots, each equipped with a fully functional Delft superconducting qubit system and an extensive set of microwave and optical interfaces, including 24 GHz and 40 GHz microwave connections, optical inputs and outputs, and infrared light access. The sample slots can be cooled using a helium-3 sorption refrigerator or a helium-4 cryorefrierator. The system's microkelvin temperature range can be achieved using a pre-cooled cryogenic magnet or by using landau level degenerate semiconductor materials. The system's design incorporates a novel magnetic field mapping system for precise field control and a set of superconducting pumps for maintaining the magnetic field. This study will particularly highlight the advantages of a helium-3 sorption refrigerator with a 10-year operational lifespan, magnetic field mapping, and superconducting pumps not found in other quantum platforms, and also outline the status of our system development, with all functional modules operational and ready for use.

From this perspective, the study examines the practical application of Cryptocurrencies and Smart Contracts by investigating misuse cases within Python code. The work begins by outlining a model that represents probable Cryptocurrencies and Smart Contracts by codifying the advice of experts, which is then used to develop a static analyzer to detect potential security risks. The analysis focuses on misuse cases such as transaction fraud, information theft, and data corruption. To assess the detector's efficacy, the authors conducted an in-depth examination of various open-source Python projects across different platforms, including GitHub and the Python Package Index, to evaluate its performance. The results demonstrate that, by categorizing detected threats as genuine or false positives (including false negatives), the detector accurately identifies a substantial number of potential security risks in popular projects. With a total of 3,775 security concerns detected, the research reveals that a notable number of these threats are legitimate risks requiring attention, while a significant portion can be disregarded as non-critical or fictitious vulnerabilities.

In modern cities, urban sound environments are diverse and vast, encompassing a wide array of sounds from everyday city life, traffic noise, and other local acoustic characteristics. This complexity makes it challenging for machines to accurately analyze and interpret city sounds. To address this issue, we developed WORTH, a system that uses a worth-based method for automatic sound tagging in urban environments. Our approach involves leveraging a city's sound taxonomy to create a worth function, which assigns different values to sounds based on their specific auditory features and the local city context. To inform this function, we collected over 200 million online polls from multiple cities, allowing us to refine sound tags through a maximum a posteriori estimation process. Our results show that WORTH outperforms current state-of-the-art tagging models, with successful applications in various urban settings, including noise complaint hotlines, cities with limited IT infrastructure, and smart cities seeking to enhance sound analysis capabilities.

We introduce a new neural network, the NuSPAN, specifically designed for the recovery of seismic reflectivity from the 1-D inverse problem using the Nonuniform Sparse Model. This problem's solution relies on a model incorporating Nonuniform Sparse total variation and a data convexification term, for which a solution exists by iteratively minimizing a proximal mean function. Building on this proximal mean function, we create the NuSPAN network, combining a convolutional layer with a reversible residual layer to expedite convergence at each iteration. Our experiments, performed on synthetic and real-world datasets, confirm NuSPAN's superiority over established techniques like FOCUSS and the 3D Deep Learning method. Furthermore, the reversible residual layer in NuSPAN enables us to develop a reusable framework for solving seismic inversion's combined model and data convexification problem, even when individual model and data terms are unavailable.

This research paper investigates a continuous semigroup of linear operators acting on specific Banach function spaces, with particular emphasis on spaces such as BMOA and its various generalizations. The semigroup in question is comprised of integral operators of the form $I-\Phi$, where $\Phi$ is a composition operator involving a analytic function $f$ on the infinite open disk $D$. The study reveals sufficient conditions for the semigroup's strong convergence on certain Banach function spaces, including BMOA and its various analogues, in relation to the behavior of the function $|f(z)-z|$ mapping from the infinite disk $D$ to the complex plane.

A crucial operator-amalgamation theorem underpins the parent-theory approach to eigenstate and ground-state algorithms, enabling the creation of highly accurate quantum eigenstate and ground state algorithms. In our study, we derive a novel operator-amalgamation expression from wavefunction overlaps, yielding crucial insights: first: nearly all parent-theory length-dependent corrections become trivial; second: a limited, universal length-d dependent correction applies widely; third: in cases where this correction is negligible, a length-independent approximation holds. Our findings are independently significant as they are applicable across a broad range of systems. To validate the general nature of our expressions, we apply and test them in the context of the Haagerup model. Specifically, we create an operator-amalgamation expression for the Haagerup model's length-d dependent correction and observe the universal, non-negligible correction in this model. Moreover, we independently derive the second-order overlap corrections in the Haagerup model and find that they are negligible. In addition to these contributions, we also leverage parent-theory length-d dependent corrections to achieve a length-d dependent approximation of the Haagerup model's critical disorder.

Accurate word classification, an essential language component, is critical for language analysis but is difficult to obtain for outdated, handwritten texts. Recent advancements in neural networks have significantly enhanced word classification accuracy, although the process remains very labor-intensive. To speed up this process, we suggest using a new method to predict word categories automatically, using an advanced deep learning technique that is well-suited for analytical tasks. This method is particularly effective for outdated texts that lack guidance words, guiding the prediction process. We tested this method using two collections from the 19th century, one from Germany and one from France, finding that it produced very reliable results, with the error rate being very low for most words.

This research paper explores a broad class of non-smooth functions that are almost everywhere well-defined. Well-known integral transforms like the Laplace and Fourier transforms do not exist for non-smooth functions lacking a neighborhood of continuity. However, we find new methods to tackle this issue by drawing on P. Koch's work on a extension of the Fourier transform applicable to non-smooth functions. Our approach extends this result to incorporate various integral transforms previously inaccessible to non-smooth functions. Moreover, it reveals connections between these transforms' existence and a range of non-smooth functions. The research also delves into the concrete case of functions with jump discontinuities, providing explicit formulas for the mentioned transforms' existence.

An increasing number of cities are utilizing autonomous vehicles and smart mobility services, leading to the need for a framework that helps establish clear guidelines for these systems. A proposed solution involves developing an AI-powered assistant that aids in creating a formal specification for these services by analyzing a city's expectations and a transportation network's properties. The proposed method utilizes a reasoning strategy to map natural language expectations into a formal specification, using a reasoning strategy to translate these expectations into a formal specification. The effectiveness of this approach was demonstrated through a case study involving a simulation of different transportation services, which showed that the assistant successfully produced an acceptable and optimal formal specification consistent with a city's needs. The proposed method was tested and validated in a real-world environment while taking into consideration the limitations and constraints of a city's needs. The proposed method was tested and validated in a real-world environment while considering several constraints that may affect a city's needs.

To eliminate errors in quantum computations, a novel method called concealed inverses is proposed. This strategy involves a single qubit correcting errors in a group of non-entangled qubits upon receipt of additional validation data from a reliable source. For example, in the case of a three-qubit photon, if the middle outcome is unknown, but the first and last are known to be correct, this new method can still provide a accurate final result without needing the middle outcome's qubit. A simulation was conducted to assess how this new method compares to conventional error correction in complex systems. Results indicate that error reduction methods can be seamlessly integrated into large-scale quantum computations, significantly minimizing overhead costs associated with validation and data transfer.

In a general category $\mathbb E$, which includes preorders and equivalence relations, a subcategory $\mathcal D$ is considered to be depictions of $\mathbb E$ if the images of the objects and arrows in $\mathcal D$ correspond to the objects and arrows in $\mathbb E$, and if the original relationships in $\mathbb E$ are preserved. In the case where $\mathbb E$ is a preorder, a subcategory $\mathcal D$ is considered correct if it satisfies certain conditions such that for any pair of objects $a$ and $b$, there exists an arrow in $\mathcal D$ from $a$ to $b$ if and only if there is an arrow in $\mathbb E$ from $a$ to $b$, and further, if an arrow in $\mathcal D$ exists from $a$ to $b$, then it represents an arrow in $\mathbb E$ from $a$ to $b$. A distinct subcategory $\mathcal C$ is introduced which includes all reflexive and symmetric epimorphisms, and it is demonstrated that a subcategory $\mathcal D$ is depictions of the preorder $\mathbb E$ if and only if $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to a subcategory $\mathcal C_{\mathcal R}$, which is based on the equivalence relations in $\mathbb E$. This research investigates the development of new multivariate spatial models for extreme value theory, specifically for analyzing high water level and wind speed interactions in coastal areas with intricate topography, characterized by significant land interaction effects on wind speed. We demonstrate the efficacy of our models through simulation studies and apply them to real-world data from the Danish coastal region, Kolind K, using a localized approach to account for the intricate relationships between sea levels and winds. This is a crucial consideration, given the potent influence of wind on sea level fluctuations.

Recently, Contrasting pre-trained image and text embeddings through Visual-Language Pre-training has received significant interest due to its capacity to learn transferable visual representations. Nevertheless, visual similarity overlaps heavily with semantic similarity, causing confusion and hindering model performance. To resolve this issue, our approach suggests incorporating multi-modal guidance during visual contrastive learning to develop more robust and accurate visual representations. We propose utilizing normalizing flows to assign meaningful text labels and matching them with images through a directional comparison, facilitated by a universal encoder. The proposed method enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of visual contrastive learning, as evidenced by our experiments on various evaluation benchmarks. Notably, VT-CLIP outperforms existing methods by a significant margin and can be effectively applied in image-text retrieval and composition.

Quantum operator matrices, when used in linear operations, are essential in computing the evolution of complex quantum systems. However, due to inevitable quantum noise, accurately calculating matrix products is challenging due to divergence. To address this issue, a universal operator matrix formulation is proposed to effectively tackle noisy systems comprising any mix of unitary, metastable, and non-unitary operators. This approach utilizes only first-order correlation functions, necessitating a storage capacity that is logarithmically related to the system's size. Furthermore, it exploits the equilibrium spectra to identify stable operator representations that are insensitive to initial conditions and capable of modeling dynamic systems. To validate this formulation, it is applied to multiple models from the quantum physics literature and compared with the results from direct numerical simulations.

Our spectral technique for detecting homotopy coherent modules is used to create 
a segmentation of stable \mathbb{Q}-Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra. This 
characterization covers all \mathbb{Q}-spectra and complements the 
classifications provided by Quillen and Adams. By applying the 
\mathbb{Q}-spectrum segmentation to the category of finite groups, we are 
able to categorize the linear \mathbb{Q}-spectra up to equivalence and 
determine the associated spectra' niches. Additionally, the segmentation 
of representable \mathbb{Q}-spectra is found to be in alignment with 
Quillen's classification of the categories of linear groups for simple 
groups and it easily extends to the general linear groups spectrum.

Given a k-rational local ring R and its prime ideal P, this paper demonstrates a connection between the k-primary ideal compactness of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial of (R,P) and the Frobenius-regularity of (R,P). Additionally, computational tools using various local cohomology modules are also provided.

The application of machine learning in image analysis is prevalent in both radiology and pathology, with ongoing research focusing on enhancing image classification and segmentation capabilities. To leverage previous research effectively, results often need to be replicated, necessitating significant time and resources. Recently, efforts to standardize image analysis outcomes have been initiated through the use of ontologies and special standardized image files, which facilitate reproducibility and data aggregation. Presently, the use of such standardization methods is ad-hoc and scattered across various studies and applications. To address this issue, we introduce Highdicom, an open-source Python library that simplifies the creation and interpretation of standardized image analysis results in dicom format. Specifically, Highdicom enables the encoding of image annotations using relevant clinical terms and generates a dicom file containing the analysis data, which can then be viewed using conventional dicom software or web browsers. To demonstrate its utility, we showcase Highdicom in two case studies, one each from the fields of radiology and pathology.

We have established that the surface area energy of a spatial section in the universe, defined by the Einstein-Hilbert action, follows the Virasoro algebra. Additionally, this system's charge, calculated using the Noether method, yields the surface area as a conserved quantity. Furthermore, this conserved quantity is linked to the entropy of the horizon, which is characterized by the time-reversal invariance of the gravitational field and follows the asymptotic time dependence of the von Neumann entropy formula.

In the realm of data mining, numerous researchers have explored the'similar sequence' problem under supervised conditions, but a crucial aspect remains understudied in unsupervised scenarios. We present an innovative method to create an intrinsic multidimensional representation of sequences akin to those employed by the human brain. Our approach relies on autoencoders, where the encoder transforms the sequence into a compact, high-dimensional format that retains the sequence's characteristics. Our research encompasses theoretical foundations, experimental results, and real-world applications. We demonstrate that this representation is versatile and can be utilized for diverse tasks such as identifying distal enhancers, categorizing sequence classes, and predicting target specificity through cross-target profiling. Additionally, our results show that enhancements like contextual data enrichment, attention-based models, and sequential ordering significantly boost the sequence's informational content in the embedding space.

Investigating the surface modification of a vanadium oxide, specifically V$_2$O$_3$, which undergoes a metal-insulator transition, is the focus of this study. Thin films were grown on a specific type of substrate and subjected to a reversible cycle of surface alteration, involving the deposition of a layer that promotes strong interactions between the films and the substrate, followed by the heat-induced sublimation of this layer. Our findings indicate that these surface changes can trigger a transition from a metastable insulating state to a stable metallic state, and this effect can be explained by the detection of visible defects on the surface of the films when they are in the insulating state, which disappear upon the surface modification. Moreover, by exposing the defect-free surface to oxygen, it is possible to restore the insulating state. These results suggest that surface conditions can significantly influence the transition into the insulating state in thin V$_2$O$_3$ films, consistent with the theoretical predictions of a two-dimensional metal-insulator model.

We're exploring new methods to solve completely integrable systems by using new representations of integrability conditions derived from symplectic frameworks.  We're developing these new representations by applying techniques from geometric quantization, specifically by taking the associated Lagrangian submanifolds as starting points.  As an application, we're able to create integrability conditions in terms of action angles for the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model through this approach, which provides a new Lie-Poisson framework.  Additionally, we're able to quantize the new framework using Kirillov's formula, which gives us a new form of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model.  We could also use this method to explore other integrable systems and give them new representations based on distinct Lie-Poisson frameworks.

The study provides an extensive analysis of all 28 confirmed planets identified by the KMTNet in 2018 in a specific field, with a focus on their characteristics, including their prime and sub-prime fields. Our research reveals significant differences between planets found in prime and sub-prime fields, with 3 out of 28 planets located in the sub-prime field exhibiting unusual characteristics. These unusual planets show large deviations from established patterns and a distinct distribution of their blue flux levels. Furthermore, a new model is proposed to better understand the relationship between planet size and their location in the host star's orbit. Based on this new model, a re-evaluation of the planetary anomalies was conducted, with interesting results showing possible correlations between certain planetary characteristics and their position in the host star's orbit.
This study implements a recently developed finite difference technique on both 2D and 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations for potential use in fluid dynamics research and applications.

This paper investigates the application of supervised machine learning techniques to data from nuclear power plants with minor incidents. A total of 11 classes were defined, corresponding to categories of minor Inadvertent Act (IA) or Minor Fault (MF) events. Applying 10 different machine learning models to the dataset, we found three models – Random Forest, Multi-layer Perceptron, and K-nearest Neighbors – to be particularly successful, achieving accuracy levels of 99.7, 99.3, and 99.6 respectively. Notably, these models surpassed the performance of a previously established model, which had achieved 98.5 accuracy. A closer examination of our study revealed that the feature selection process had produced consistent results, underscoring the importance of certain physical features, including sound, temperature, and pressure metrics, in predicting IA and MF events.

Two approaches, respectively based on q-rook theory and fully symmetric function expansion, are employed to derive a combinatorial interpretation of $e_{(p)}\cdot \text{Dyer}_n(\lambda)$, where $e_{(p)}$ represents a colored inverse shift operator, $\text{Dyer}_n(\lambda)$ symbolizes a Dyck path colored symmetry function with partition $\lambda$, and $e_{(p)}$ acts on $\text{Dyer}_n(\lambda)$ to shift its colorings by a shift number related to $p$, which can be seen as both a generalization of the $q$-rook settlement formula in terms of fully symmetric function language, and the coloring analog of the $q$-queens theorem.

Convolutional Neural Networks, notably those with VGG-like architectures, have become industry standards for image classification tasks. However, they are not without limitations, particularly when dealing with images that have been altered by rotations. This issue can be rectified through the incorporation of orientation-enhancing components within Convolutional Neural Networks. Such a modification not only enhances the network's ability to detect rotated objects, but also improves its overall performance on rotation-insensitive image classification tasks. Our research indicates that our novel architecture, ORIENT-CNN, consistently outperforms leading competitors like VGG and RotNet, achieving superior results on rotation-sensitive image classification tasks.

A generalised version of the trace equation is derived for arbitrary curved linear profiles with a non-zero derivative. We demonstrate its application in determining fundamental parameters of light curves and maps, which is particularly useful in their representation. The equation is also relevant to the field of map representation, where it allows for a unique determination of parameters given a map and its associated trace.

In our study, we investigated the top quark's significant contribution to the strong top quark interaction, focusing on its connection to the strong coupling constant and parton distribution functions.  The model we used encompasses all significant aspects of QCD corrections within a factor of approximation and is independent of the specific details in the standard model regarding the treatment of loop masses, CKM matrix elements, and cabibbo-kobayashi-maskawa matrix elements.  The model's top quark mass distribution is expressed in terms of the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ mass, and our results are applicable to any scenario with a non-zero top quark mass even when considering flavor changing neutral currents.  The model's purpose is to provide a useful approximation for calculating direct Higgs production via gluon fusion, and our results are particularly useful for calculations at next-to-minimal supersymmetric model (NMSSM) type and in scenarios with universal extra dimensions with a diagonal flavor structure at next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy.

Consecutive edge-tinting on a graph G of order n involves dividing its vertices into two groups, denoted by R and B, such that the edges incident on adjacent vertices of R are colored red, while those incident on adjacent vertices of B are colored blue. If G has a conjugate pair of subsets of vertices with size n/2, where the subsets R and B satisfy this condition, we define the conjugacy degree of G to be the maximum possible value of this color assignment. This problem's research focus, which is largely driven by graph theory, has significant theoretical value. Our study begins by identifying the conjugacy degree for all integers n and 2n the vertices of order have, specifically, 4k (k greater than or equal to 2) and (k greater than or equal to 1) with some additional constraints. These include the possibility of two colored squares forming a grid, a property which is unique to k equal to 3, and for all k, the existence of a cycle with a length of 2k that is contained within the graph. Furthermore, it was observed that when k is greater than or equal to 4, the maximum possible size of the independent set in the graph is 5k. This research was found to be related to a problem in beacons and intercovering sets.

We prove a hypercontractive inequality for scaled Bergman spaces over various complex regions, including all convex domains with a power type boundary behavior. In addition, this hypercontractive inequality leads to the boundedness of a Bergman type operator for functions over such regions, including those with a boundary behavior described by a power function with a positive coefficient. This result resolves an open question posed by Paluszynski and Stollenwerk. Furthermore, this hypercontractive inequality has practical implications for a similar operator applied to functions over sufficiently convex domains that is bounded to yield a bounded outcome.

Currently, the most reliable methods for identifying COVID-19 from chest X-rays involve deep learning models trained on extensive datasets. However, the scarcity of imaging data in some regions necessitates the development of more efficient algorithms that can excel in detecting the disease from fewer, higher quality X-ray images. To address this challenge, we have collected a comprehensive dataset of 14,188 radiology reports from multiple institutions in China, and selected 8,042 enhanced CT scans from this pool. Our innovative, two-stage capsule network design specializes in detecting COVID-19 in noisy chest X-rays. First, it utilizes capsule modules in a convolutional neural network to extract spatially consistent features from raw input images. Next, it employs a capsule network that incorporates spatial and temporal information from previously-identified positive patches within the image. Our capsule network design outperforms current state-of-the-art models, achieving an accurate diagnosis of COVID-19 from these enhanced CT scans (86.4% for 5-fold cross-validation) and even from standard, low-quality chest X-rays (79.6% for 5-fold cross-validation). Moreover, the framework is highly modular and easily modifiable, which facilitates the incorporation of multiple positive patches, the exploitation of spatial temporal relationships, and the integration of traditional symptom-based diagnosis. Due to its versatility, this model can be adapted for use on various scanning machines and in diverse data collections. Our research has far-reaching implications, as it lays the groundwork for the development of a portable

A growing number of commercial satellites are being launched into Low-Earth Orbit, which has become the preferred destination for a wide range of spacecraft. With numerous satellites already occupying this orbit and more being deployed, various organizations are working to develop strategies for tracking and utilizing the available space to maximize their operational capabilities. In support of these efforts, a new study is launching a comprehensive survey to gather information from stakeholders, which will inform the development of practical tools and methodologies to aid mission planners in finding suitable locations within the orbit for satellite operations to begin.

Research in computer-aided engineering has extensively utilized mesh optimization to improve various tasks, and optimizing mesh order has emerged as a crucial aspect. To address this issue, a method is proposed which formulates the problem as an optimization task to enforce whole number constraints on the mesh variable. The variable in question represents the mapping of vertices from a coarse quadrilateral mesh to their corresponding precise representations on a model. By treating these mappings as variables, higher order mesh creation becomes possible, and this approach allows for handling complex topological relationships between vertices. Notably, this method does not rely on approximations often found in other methods, and instead provides an exact solution to the optimization task, resulting in optimal mesh distances with a whole number value. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through various numerical experiments, and the results show that it compares favorably to other methods in terms of quality and efficiency.

To assess the correlation between two variables, one can utilize the sample correlation based on observed data points. The sample correlation is calculated as the product of the sample standard deviations of the two variables and the sample Pearson's correlation coefficient. This study develops theoretical expressions for the moments of the sample correlation coefficient, evaluated at specific configuration points of data, such as the median, where the sample correlation coefficient is most stable. The obtained expressions are then employed to establish a confidence interval for the sample correlation coefficient. The sample correlation coefficient's performance is evaluated under distinct data distributions, including the normal distribution and a specific non-normal distribution, at a median-based configuration. The results indicate that the proposed confidence interval surpasses the traditional ones, especially for cases involving non-normal distributions, thus showing improved reliability.

We detail the reasoning behind implementing the $S$-matrix formulation of the fundamental theory of physics, along with its effectiveness in uncovering general relativity and the subsequent discovery of black holes. Additionally, the document outlines the current advancements in developing a theory that succeeds general relativity based on the $S$-matrix approach.

We investigate the two- or three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations defined within a bounded region. This model takes into account an external force that is assumed to be controlled, and we focus on stabilizing the velocity and pressure functions, denoted as $u$ and $p$, through feedback control, specifically on the velocity. This control is implemented in a finite dimensional space within the interior of the region. By this mechanism, the system can be stabilized uniformly in a range of Sobolev and Besov spaces based on $L^q$-norm, provided the input data satisfy a specific condition denoted as $q_0$. This condition is such that when $q > q_0$, the space associated with the $L^q$-norm is critically embedded in the space associated with the $L^p$-norm, and when $q < q_0$, the space associated with the $L^q$-norm is not critically embedded in the space associated with the $L^p$-norm. This work significantly improves upon a previously developed theory by removing the requirement that the external force be smooth and provides a more precise estimate of the velocity and its time decay. This outcome is illustrated through concrete examples in which the input data do not satisfy the required smoothness condition or may even be zero in a neighborhood of the boundary of the region. The LitMind Lexicon is a comprehensive dictionary of contemporary Chinese, consisting of 55,000+ entries and 620,000+ definitions, which can be accessed at https://litmind.org/. This lexicon is distinct from other dictionaries in two key ways: Firstly, it prioritizes the everyday words people use in their daily lives, focusing on common rather than complex or obscure language. Secondly, it includes definitions written in a more natural sentence structure, which is intended to facilitate easier understanding and be more engaging for the reader. This lexicon is designed to be a dynamic resource that can be modified directly by users, with all data being openly accessible via the Git repository at https://github.com/LitMind/LitMind-Dict.

To foster trust in Autonomous Decision-Making Systems, particularly those found in Recommendations, it's crucial that their decisions and reasoning be both understandable to humans and aligned with human values. To address this, researchers have proposed various methods for making complex models more transparent, with PTP-RS and LIME-RS being two notable approaches for high-interaction and low-interaction systems respectively, although they exhibit a crucial limitation in ensuring generated feature-focusing interpretations align with actual user values and system internals. In response, a new approach is presented, aiming to improve upon LIME-RS by being compliant with system internals and stable across different evaluations, with evaluation results showing positive trends on Amazon Catalogue and Last.FM datasets.

Indium arsenide quantum wells are considered a viable alternative to the more expensive and difficult to manufacture indium antimonide quantum wells, offering potential advantages through the use of an optimized surface treatment process called fermi level fixation. Our study employed x-ray photoemission spectroscopy to thoroughly examine the fermi level fixation process in indium arsenide quantum wells with two different layers of indium. We found that the surface treatment is successful in creating a distinct interface between the indium and the semiconductor, but this does not necessarily mean it leads to a complete separation between the covalent and free carrier components of the valence band maximum. In fact, the free carrier component appears to persist even after the treatment, but the surface treatment does succeed in reducing the width of the quantum well, thereby increasing the energy gap between the conduction and valence band edges. We also discovered that the surface treatment alters the composition of the surface layers, causing them to become rich in arsenic. This arsenic-rich layer may have the potential to serve as a separate layer in the quantum well, similar to what is seen in indium antimonide quantum wells and offers the possibility of further reducing the width of the quantum well through the use of an optimized surface treatment.

In deep neural networks, localizing errors due to adversarial attacks can be achieved through regional queries, where the network repeatedly computes outputs for smaller subsets of the input pixel values. However, this research suggests that regional queries can also be utilized as an auxiliary training method to enhance resilience, and the key factor influencing its effectiveness is the selected layer to apply this technique. We found that training with regional queries from earlier layers increases the loss they produce during regularization, and this leads to better resilience in the interior of the network and lower robustness to edge pixels. Additionally, this technique has a minimal impact on model accuracy. Based on these findings, we recommend training models with regional queries starting from the third layer or later.

Our previous research, Detailed Sinkhorn, significantly enhanced the computational efficiency of the Sinkhorn algorithm via data compression and reduced precision, now further optimized with a novel solution approach that exploits structural relationships within the optimal transport problem. Specifically, a O(n) algorithm has been developed for determining optimal transport costs without rounding errors and a corresponding O(n log n) scheme for computing optimal transport maps, both of which rely on a column-oriented, triangular data structure. This improved framework is now known as Rapid Sinkhorn. To facilitate faster convergence, a more robust iterative scheme has been created and analysis has been conducted to determine the relationship between the accuracy of the initial estimate of the optimal transport cost and the number of iterations required. Consequently, Rapid Sinkhorn is capable of rapidly solving large-scale optimal transport problems with single-precision floating point numbers, specifically in about m times the number of precision steps in our previous work, thereby enabling the solution of problems with up to 100 times more variables than before.

AU Mic is a young stellar object exhibiting intense starburst events characterized by massive dust ejections that can be seen propagating through space at remarkable speeds. Previous observations of the object revealed powerful starburst events in the ultraviolet spectrum that greatly surpassed expectations set by models of young stellar objects. Studies of AU Mic, a young star with two planets located about 32 light years away, have shown that its dust ejection events may have significant implications for understanding planetary system evolution. Our team conducted a comprehensive analysis based on a large dataset of FUV observations of AU Mic, spanning from 1991 to 2022, which was gathered using the IUE, FUSE, HST/STIS, and HST/COS telescopes. Our observations showed that, in its dormant state, AU Mic's FUV spectrum matches predictions set by models of a Peculiars T Tauri Star, but this changed during its 2003 FUV eruption when its spectrum deviated significantly, exhibiting characteristics more similar to those of a young, hot white dwarf. Our analysis also enabled us to update previous estimates for the object: a dust mass of about 5 x 10^(-5) solar masses was calculated for the 2003 eruption, while a speed of about 10 km/s was recorded for the dust ejection. Our observations, however, showed that high speeds for the ejection were only achieved at later stages, after it had interacted with the surrounding material, unlike predictions

When carriers in a semiconductor are exposed to ionizing radiation, it causes two main effects: it generates electron-hole pairs, creating an increased current, and it increases the material's resistance to conduction. This phenomenon has two distinct components, electron and ion motion, which respectively contribute to the increased current and resistance. The electron component is well-documented but the ion component is less understood. This article initially reviews the principles of radiation response drag then explores a specific situation where a resistive layer is immersed in a material with increased radiation response. The article provides mathematical expressions for this material's increased resistance under radiation, a larger effect than that produced by the increased current, and predicts the material's resistance to conduction will be maximized at an optimal radiation dose.

For high-dimensional, sparse datasets with an imbalance of class sizes, traditional classification methods can be unreliable in their predictions. The nearest neighbor classification is particularly susceptible to outliers and noise, making it a less favorable option. In this context, a refined closest neighbor classification (ReFiniCN) algorithm is introduced, which incorporates a weight adjustment mechanism to compensate for the influence of more common minorities when classifying uneven datasets. The system's reliability under various real-world data conditions has been thoroughly tested. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms the existing literature, exhibiting greater accuracy and lower variance across multiple types of imbalanced datasets. The method's effectiveness has also been supported by comparative simulations with standard nearest neighbor classification, indicating its potential as a superior base learner in ensemble learning.

These QSOs, both extremely luminous and very distant, have been found. In a specific light band (u-g color), a relationship with their luminosity has been established, specifically those highly luminous QSOs, with a peak occurring around 260nm, are rarer. On the basis of this, a specific group of QSOs, with the most luminous QSOs, z~5, have been found. Our study delves into the interactions between a quantum point contact and a superconducting island within a hybrid device that incorporates a quantum Hall system and a superconducting island via a back gate. Utilizing radio-frequency spectroscopy, we identify specific mechanisms through which charge fluctuations occur: primary factors include localized extra quasiparticle tunneling, 1/f noise, and random telegraph signals originating from the quantum point contact itself. Notably, we observe that the primary tunneling mechanism can shift in response to applied alignment voltages, demonstrating control over these interactions. Furthermore, we explore the influence of these interactions on the quantum point contact's local density fluctuations.

Recent research on hyperbolic systems of conservation laws has introduced a new class of behaviors known as "entropic discontinuities." The basis of this development lies in a standard for contraction, which is required for time-evolution operators to function effectively in the context of the context of metric spaces. The paper provides a detailed description of standards for contraction with respect to complete metrics, which include the weakly backward metric and the Brouwer metric. It further demonstrates that certain norms associated with the Brouwer metric exhibit a singular property - they are continuous only when approached from a specific direction. Moreover, numerical examples have shown that the class of entropic discontinuities is particularly significant for a certain type of non-linear system, which fails to experience similar contraction behaviors under the use of certain metrics.

To manufacture imaginary landscapes, we need high-quality, infinite view synthesis techniques that generate accurate and consistent predictions. However, current approaches using deep learning models have limitations, particularly in their ability to maintain consistency and accuracy in predictions that extend beyond the original field of view. These limitations can result in the generation of unrealistic and distorted images. To address this challenge, we have developed a novel conditional diffusion model, DiffDreamer, which leverages a memory mechanism to maintain consistency and accuracy in predictions across various scenarios. Our approach also enables the generation of synthetic images with diverse infinite views, and these images are indistinguishable from real images. Additionally, DiffDreamer has the ability to seamlessly transition between top-view and side-view perspectives of a scene. We have conducted thorough experiments to validate the effectiveness of our approach, and these experiments demonstrate the ability of DiffDreamer to significantly outperform existing methods in both reliability and realism.

Many complex dynamic systems are hidden within a large network of interconnected components. Studying these systems is often a daunting task due to their highly nonlinear and sensitive nature. In this research, a cutting-edge approach is presented for modeling, analyzing, and controlling complex systems through a data analysis method that uses graph theory. This data analysis method automatically detects the underlying network structure, characterizes the dynamics, and prescribes control policies with minimal external influence. In a large-scale epidemic model known as the networked SIS model, this research demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach by predicting outbreaks, improving predictive accuracy, and regulating dynamics using non-invasive interventions. These results showcase the value of our approach in understanding, managing, and controlling complex systems through graphical analysis.

The Rayleigh-Plateau instability occurs when a liquid column is reduced in size, leading to the dissociation of drops and larger cylinders into smaller segments. Our research examines how the boundary slipping into solid surfaces influences the Rayleigh-Plateau instability. We began by studying the dynamics of a solitary drop on a surface with boundary slipping using the Stokes equation for fluids, formulating an expression for the contact angle that considers boundary slipping. We discovered that a drop undergoes evaporation-driven shape changes similar to those of a liquid droplet undergoing gravity-driven flow when the boundary slipping coefficient is large. We developed an approximation for the boundary driven Rayleigh-Plateau instability by combining both the gravitational and boundary slipping effects. We found that the onset of instability is determined by the correlation between the two effects, with changes in the boundary slipping coefficient and drop aspect ratios resulting in distinct instability types. Our model, although derived for a single drop, can also be applied to larger liquid layers on fibers, revealing that boundary slipping accelerates the onset of instability. We provided a criterion for estimating the boundary driving effect based on the boundary slipping coefficient, changing relative velocities, and geometry ratios. This criterion facilitated a comparison between experiments and our model, revealing good correspondence between them.

Researchers have been actively working in the area of regularization techniques derived from Lipschitz stability. The concept gained its initial insights from anisotropic curvature flows like the Hamiltonian identity and the Hunter-Saxton formula. This study focuses on the Lipschitz stability of the Hunter-Saxton formula and introduces a definition of Lipschitz stability for a broad category of PDEs, including those that may not be strictly hyperbolic. Furthermore, the study discusses the properties of solutions to the Hunter-Saxton formula, proves its local Lipschitz continuity, and explores the relationships between its solutions and 1-dentable measures. The study also establishes that for a measure μ having 1-dentable tangency levels at x0, the (HT)(t, μ) remains Lipschitz continuous for all t ≥ 0.

A new method called USpiny was recently developed to automate ultrasound spine imaging using a robotic scanner moved along a fixed trajectory. This technique allows for continuous ultrasound imaging without having to reposition the transducer, which is essential for assessing scoliosis and spine deformities. To evaluate its reliability, a study was conducted to assess the consistency of USpiny in measuring spinal curvature in a standard and dynamic setting. Compared to a human-operated scanner, robotic scanning exhibited equivalent spinal curvature measurements (within a 10-degree margin of error) and demonstrated greater precision (by 3 degrees). Furthermore, robotic scanning enabled scoliosis angle measurements with the transducer positioned more freely and freely allowed for more comprehensive spinal coverage (by 10% area increase). These results demonstrate that robotic scanning can be a reliable approach for evaluating spinal curvature, particularly when combined with flexible transducer positioning.

This research introduces a novel, medians-driven technique for generating speech
lengths that are both concise and expandable for any given language, which can
be implemented without access to language-specific statistical data. The core
objective of this innovation is to precisely control the length of the speech
synthesis output. To achieve this goal, a in-depth analysis was conducted of
speech correlation patterns at varying length intervals, spanning the range of
5 to 300 seconds. Our findings revealed that speech characteristics can be
effectively categorized into distinct categories based on length. Furthermore,
corresponding results demonstrated the feasibility of applying the medians-
driven method in conjunction with a statistical model to produce synthesized
speech of a natural, randomized character.

This research explores the utilization of Hate Speech Wedge Characteristic Extraction in detecting online hate speech content. The online platform has served as a breeding ground for hate speech due to its ease of distribution and global accessibility via social media. However, it also presents difficulties in characterizing the sentiment and classification of this type of content due to its complex nature and rapid evolution. Our model has overcome these challenges by incorporating Hate Speech Wedge Characteristic Extraction, which is based on the theory of online hate speech dynamics as a geometric shape with three distinct sections: Ignorance, Indifference, and Hostility. Our solution is an end-to-end model that combines BERT, NLP techniques such as Part-of-Speech and sentence embedding along with DL specific layers to extract distinctive features from online hate speech data, thus outperforming current standards in the field. Our model's effectiveness was validated using a comprehensive dataset comprising text and image data, cross-checked with existing datasets to ensure its broad applicability. Our proposed model's capabilities were tested using the BERT-NLI model that integrates NLP techniques, thus breaking new ground in the field of online hate speech detection. Our results show that this model can be used effectively in other hazardous environments such as online terrorist content detection.

In multi-input multi-output systems, the internal units distribute information
through interconnected edges, and to facilitate feature exchange between different
paths, MIMO architectures rely on specific structural designs such as shared
layers and parallel branches. However, increasing the complexity of feature exchanging
strategies does not always lead to better performance, and simpler methods can be more
efficient. This study focuses on various feature exchanging techniques within MIMO
frameworks and evaluates their impact on model scalability and adaptability. Through
experimental analysis, the paper demonstrates the advantages of effective feature
exchanging in enhancing model performance and highlights the importance of selecting
appropriate exchanging strategies to optimize MIMO structures.

This study examines the evolution of institutional partnerships in digitizing historical manuscript collections, focusing on the pivotal role of collaborative digitization and the importance of institutional input in the creation of quality digital collections. It ultimately positions the development of the Model Archival Dataset (MAD), a recently introduced benchmark standard for manuscript image compression and compression analysis.

A significant drawback of model-based control for industrial robots is the inability to adapt to discrepancies between the predicted and actual models. Our proposed method addresses this limitation by developing a novel feedback system that relies on positional information rather than joint position. The main objective of this system is to ensure the end-effector maintains a consistent orientation throughout its trajectory, which is particularly crucial for certain applications. A flatness-based approach is implemented to design the feedback system, and simulation results are presented to demonstrate its effectiveness. Moreover, an experimental implementation of the system on a ABB 120da robot arm using additional sensors is described, highlighting potential methods for sensor data interpretation.

A comprehensive approach is being developed to study the long-term health effects of individuals who have experienced a specific serious illness. This strategy is based on an innovative analytical framework, which assesses multiple stages of health development in people who have had and not had the serious illness, using a statistical method that incorporates the serious illness as one of the multiple factors under study. An analysis of individuals who have had a myocardial infarction or a similar serious cardiovascular condition, in comparison to those who have not experienced such a serious illness, is used to demonstrate the effectiveness of this new analysis method in its initial application. An enhanced picture of long-term health outcomes in people who have had the serious illness is gained through this new analysis, which identifies additional conditions beyond those typically expected for this group. Additionally, this new analysis reveals differences in the progression of long-term health effects between people who have had the serious illness and those who have not. Finally, by studying both groups using the new analysis method, the stage at which long-term health effects typically occur can be more accurately identified.

The electronic structure of molecules is fundamentally determined by the resolution of the one-electron density functions described by the Schrödinger and Hartree equations. Historically, numerical methods have been used more frequently in theoretical molecular science than experimental techniques.

This article presents a multi-site quadrature approach, where a subset of basis elements transforms into a quadrature-based basis. We demonstrate that the associated matrix is orthogonal and, in the special case where the basis is partitioned equally, is unitary. Furthermore, the proposed quadrature matrix for a given dimension and number of quadrature points has a greater determinant than its counterpart for a d-dimensional hypercube.

We illustrate the properties of the proposed quadrature when applied to a continuous setting. Additionally, some intriguing connections to the fermion infinite-dimensional clifford algebra are also discussed.

In a graph, a subset of vertices forms a resolving set if, for any two vertices, a single set vertex is positioned at different distances from the two vertices.  A subset's size is referred to as the metric dimension of the graph.  We investigated how to parameterize resolving set size using specific structural attributes : feedback vertex number, split vertices, leaf number, and treedepth.  Within each of these attributes, we established parameterized complexity results for various problem variants, including decision, fixed parameter, and fixed value problems.  These results demonstrate new applications of specific complexity tools, such as the Crossing Number demotion technique, as well as the Excluded Grid H-minor parameterized by treedepth.

A new type of directed area for vector fields on orientable two-dimensional manifolds is introduced, and its relationship with a known measure of direction is explored. The properties of this new measure, denoted as the 'p-regularity', are investigated in relation to a weighted version of the underlying manifold. The existence of a directed area invariant under volume-preserving homeomorphisms is demonstrated, and it is shown that this new type of directed area forms a Banach space when paired with a suitable norm, denoted as a 'p-space'. The development of integration theories for directed areas and their application to generalized flow maps are also presented. The work concludes with a consideration of the infinitesimal properties of this new type of directed area in a manifold tangent space.

To analyze how intense rainfalls might alter the Earth's climate, we studied liquid droplet accumulation and fluid flow in simplified greenhouse-like atmospheres with high temperatures and pressures. Our model accounts for vapor and heat dynamics, and uses a novel numerical approach that preserves accuracy in critical areas where solutions can become unstable. The numerical technique, based on an existing finite difference method, ensures positive fluid volumes while maintaining convergence. We observed that, in certain cases, the convergence of the solutions depends on the specific conditions being modeled and always occurs even if the conditions change rapidly. Our research focused on the long-term behavior of the solutions under different scenarios and found that, ultimately, the solutions settle into a predictable pattern of periodic rainfall and a steady, high level of atmospheric moisture. The study also revealed that the rate of vapor condensation at the bottom of the atmosphere plays a critical role in this pattern and that increased rainfalls can lead to more consistent behavior and a more stable overall climate.

We have set up an infinite set of twistors, called twistor creations, for various Yang-Mills theories with higher and higher spins, as well as their self-dual counterparts. These self-dual theories have four-spin values, sitting at the top of a SO(4)N representation, while the non-self-dual theories have two-spin values, sitting at the top of a (gl(N|gl(H))-action) representation. These twistors exist in a space with an infinite number of degrees of freedom, denoted as V_infinity. When the spin value is half-integrated, the twistor creations transform under supersymmetry, according to a (gl(N|gl(H)) supersymmetry transformation. The twistor creations for higher and higher spins can be generated through a free fermion operator, which carries either spin 1/2 or 3/2. This operator, denoted as psi, has a non-local behavior when the spin value becomes very large. The twistor creations for self-dual higher-spin Yang-Mills theories, when applied to flat space, imply that higher-spin gauge fields, when the spin value exceeds three, become non-local objects. However, this analysis only applies to flat space. When the space becomes curved, one needs to use the supersymmetric twistor creation for (gl(N)|gl(H)) and an invariant Lagrangian must be formulated based on the non-local twistors.
